proof.criterion: Architect's item 4 — internal/testpg.Drop only drops the test databases and cannot touch any other database.
proof.surface: The Go test helper every daemon suite's teardown runs against whatever PostgreSQL LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN names, including the shared one each Legion pod uses.
proof.command: grep -rn 'testpg\.Drop' --include=*.go . ; then, per caller, how its name is built
proof.observed: It cannot. `Drop(ctx, admin, name)` executes `drop database <name> with (force)` — the same statement as before, unchanged; all this round added is a retry on SQLSTATE 42501 and a 30-second bound. The blast radius is therefore the set of names callers pass, and I read every one: eleven call sites repo-wide (the definition's own `t.Cleanup` in testpg.go:59, plus ten in `_test.go` files). Every one passes a name its own helper created moments earlier in the same function, of the form `<literal prefix>_<hex of 8 crypto/rand bytes>` — `legion_record_test_`, `legion_api_test_`, `legion_sandbox_test_`, `dispatch_outbox_test_` and so on — immediately after `create database <that name>`, and each drop is that creation's own `t.Cleanup`. No caller takes a database name from configuration, from the environment, or from the DSN: `Database()` parses LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN only to reach the admin database and to build the returned URL, never to choose what to drop. So a drop can only ever name a database the same test just created, and the random suffix means it can never collide with a database anything else made.
proof.negativeControl: The retry's own narrowness is the control, and it is in the code rather than in a run: `Drop` returns the error unchanged unless `errors.As` finds a `*pgconn.PgError` whose `Code` is exactly `42501`, so every other refusal — a database that does not exist, a name the login may not drop — ends the call at once rather than being retried for thirty seconds. I could not reproduce the 42501 itself in this pod: my harness runs PostgreSQL with a superuser login, which is allowed to terminate the autovacuum backend, so the condition never arises here. The pod's shared `legion_test` login is where it bites, and CI runs as the container's superuser and never sees it — which is why this was invisible to CI and red in the pod.
